It differs from standard NeRF by encoding smooth density and UV coordinates in a 3D feature volume while storing detailed appearance in a 2D Neural Texture Stack (NTS), enabling real-time performance and retexturing [S1].

The claim states that the method differs from standard NeRF by encoding smooth density and UV coordinates in a 3D feature volume while storing detailed appearance in a 2D Neural Texture Stack (NTS), enabling real-time performance and retexturing. Source [S1] explicitly confirms all these points: it mentions separating high-frequency appearance from the 3D volume, encoding smooth UV volumes (containing density and UV coordinates) in 3D, using a 2D Neural Texture Stack (NTS) for detailed appearance, achieving real-time performance (30FPS), and enabling retexturing.

Therefore, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.

UV Volumes is a method for real-time, editable free-view rendering of human performers that decouples smooth 3D geometry and density from high-frequency appearance [S1].

The claim states that UV Volumes is a method for real-time, editable free-view rendering of human performers that decouples smooth 3D geometry and density from high-frequency appearance. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly supports every part of this claim: 1) It describes UV Volumes as a new approach to render an 'editable free-view video of a human performer in real-time'. 2) It states the method 'separates the highfrequency (i.e., non-smooth) human appearance from the 3D volume'. 3) It explains that 'smooth UV volumes' are used to obtain 'densities and texture coordinates in 3D' while capturing 'detailed appearance in 2D NTS', which corresponds to decoupling smooth geometry/density from high-frequency appearance.
